results.content: Consumer sentiment plunged in September amid heightened inflation fears, hitting its second-lowest level on record in the University of Michigan’s monthly survey released Friday. The survey’s headline index hit a level of 47.8, down 7.5% from the August reading and off 13.2% from a year ago. This was the second-lowest reading on record for data going back to 1952 — the bottom coming in May as rising prices also jolted the outlook. Indeed, the one-year inflation outlook surged to 4.6%, up 0.6 percentage point from the prior level and the highest since hitting the same level in June. results.content: President Donald Trump’s approval rating found a sort of oasis in the desert, rising after weeks of record lows, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll released on Monday, Sept. The poll found that 35% of Americans approved of the president's job performance, up two percentage points from the previous Reuters/Ipsos tracking poll released in early September. Trump’s slight improvement in the newest poll came after three straight weeks of the lowest approval numbers he had seen in Reuters/Ipsos tracking since his return to the White House in 2025.
